newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Cambodia's aid donors urged not to pull the plug.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's aid donors urged not to pull the plug.

text.p: Foreign aid donors to Cambodia should not withold their support to the politically troubled country, but should funnel the funds directly to the people, Association of South East Asian Nation (ASEAN) academics and officials said on Wednesday.
"We all know that this (foreign aid) is extremely crucial to Cambodia," said Mohamed Jawhar Hassan, director-general of think-tank Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia.

"It is in fact many ways a lifeline of Cambodia and Cambodians...it is in the interest of Cambodia that the assistance continues," Jawhar told an ASEAN congress of diplomats, businessmen and academics.
But he added that the monies should be given "to the people...to the projects they are meant for and not to the regime to perpetuate itself".
A bloody coup in early July in which Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh prompted the United States to suspend all bilateral aid for 30 days.

Cambodia gets half its annual budget from overseas donations, with Japan providing about half of the aid amount. Donor countries pledged $450 million to Cambodia at a meeting in Paris earlier this month.
Last year, Cambodia received $500 million in aid.

The United States allocated $35 million in aid to Cambodia for fiscal 1997, which ends in September. It has said that after the 30 days, it may keep operating parts of the aid programme that benefit Cambodia's people but not the government.
The attempt to rid Cambodia of land mines is one of those programmes.
Australia said it was halting military aid while leaving alone A$32 million (US$23.7 million) a year in general aid.

"We understand it (foreign aid) is not a Cambodian entitlement," Kao Kim Hourn, executive director of the Cambodian Institute for Cooperation and Peace, told the ASEAN congress, which met ahead of the 30th anniversary meetings of the regional grouping.
ASEAN on Wednesday reaffirmed its decision to postpone Cambodia's membership in the group, now enlarged to nine with the admission of Burma and Laos.
ASEAN, celebrating its 30th year, now comprises Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam, the Philippines, Brunei, Burma and Laos.
